obligations.note: The new branch in is_allowed allows any action of the form "report:<action>" for roles granted <action>. These strings are not in ACTIONS, the explicit GRANTS or the approved access policy, so grants are no longer decided explicitly or denied by default; for example, treasury_manager is now allowed "report:release_payment". The exhaustive control test enumerates only the declared roles x actions and cannot see this alias namespace.

The alias only mirrors existing grants, and auditor holds no state-changing base action, so no "report:" alias gives auditor a state-changing action. test_auditor_is_read_only passed on the head commit.
it_admin holds neither approve_payment nor release_payment, so the alias cannot grant them. test_it_admin_cannot_approve_or_release passed on the head commit.
Ticket CHG-24775 is standard and was approved by change manager Erik Brandt at 2026-10-18T00:44Z, before review. Its components (payments.access) cover rbac.py.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver and not the author, gave a code_review approval.
The code_review and security_review approvals both name the head commit 82712f6, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json claims a run on head by ci-runner-07. The only JUnit report, however, is timestamped 2026-10-23, after the review time of 2026-10-20, and came from host dev-laptop-7.local. It is therefore not valid evidence from the change's own CI run, and no other report shows the suite passing on the final commit.
rbac.py (payments.access) is security_sensitive. Kofi Mensah, a security_reviewer, approved a security_review on the head commit.
The register has no exception for ACC-1 on payments.access, so the default-deny deviation is not covered by any approved exception.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers rbac.py. The covered code (payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and the mortgage files) is unchanged, so no evidence lapses.

summary: The change adds a "report:" prefix alias in rbac.is_allowed that grants actions outside the explicit, approved grants matrix. This breaks ACC-1's explicit-decision and default-deny requirement, and no exception covers it. The CI evidence is also inconsistent: the JUnit report is dated after the review time and comes from a personal workstation rather than the recorded CI runner. Ticket, independent approval and security review are otherwise in order, but the change must be rejected.
